Claude responded: ML engineer

Comparing AI and ML engineering career paths in India.
Comparing AI and ML engineering career paths in India.

ML engineer

An ML engineer builds and trains models. The work includes data pipelines, feature engineering, training and evaluating models, and getting them into production (MLOps). It needs stronger fundamentals: statistics, linear algebra, classical ML, deep learning, and a good grasp of why a model behaves the way it does. Typical employers are product companies, fintech, e-commerce, and anywhere with lots of proprietary data (recommendations, fraud detection, forecasting).

AI engineer

An AI engineer builds applications on top of existing models, mostly LLMs and other foundation models accessed through APIs or open-weight checkpoints. The work includes prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agents and tool use, evaluation, fine-tuning when needed, and wiring it all into a real product with good latency, cost, and reliability. It’s closer to software engineering with a strong AI layer. Typical employers are startups, IT services firms, and product teams adding AI features.

The core difference: ML engineers mostly make models, while AI engineers mostly use models to make products. The titles are used loosely, and many job postings blur them, so always read the actual job description.

Which should a fresher in India choose?

My suggestion is to not treat it as a permanent either/or choice, but to pick an entry point:

  • If you’re a strong coder and like building things, start on the AI engineer side. There are more entry-level openings of this kind, since many Indian IT services companies and startups are shipping LLM-based features, and you can build a portfolio quickly (a RAG app, an agent, an evaluation harness).
  • If you enjoy math and statistics, or are doing a degree or research with that depth, go the ML engineer route. Roles are fewer and more competitive for freshers, and employers often prefer a strong academic background, but the skills are more durable and transfer well.
  • If you’re unsure, build a base that serves both: Python, solid software engineering (Git, APIs, SQL, testing, cloud basics), core ML concepts, and then one or two real projects deployed end to end. Recruiters respond to shipped projects far more than to course certificates.

One practical point is that “AI engineer” is the newer and more hype-driven title, so check that a role involves real engineering and not just calling an API. And since this field changes quickly, check current openings on LinkedIn, Naukri, and Wellfound for your target cities before committing to a path, as demand shifts from year to year.

If you tell me your degree, current skills, and what you enjoy (math, building apps, research), I can suggest a more specific learning roadmap.
